entry.name: Robbers in the Samaritan parable
entry.note: Unnamed group inside Jesus’s story in Luke 10:30 who attack the traveler and depart. Distinct from the men crucified with Jesus and all other robbery groups. Describe a typical member.

result.appearanceFromText: The text names only 'robbers' who stripped and beat the traveler and departed; it fixes no physical features, so the look is supplied from the Roman-era Judean roadside setting, with rough tunics and cloaks typical of the period.

stages.label: Robbers (typical member)
stages.when: Roman Judea, the road from Jerusalem down to Jericho

quotes.quote: he fell among robbers, who both stripped him and beat him, and departed

stages.text: Robbers: a typical member is a lean adult man, aged late twenties to forties, of wiry build with weathered olive skin, dark hair and short beard. He wears a faded earth-brown tunic belted at the waist with a dusty cloak of undyed wool and sandals or bare feet. Signature props carried alone: a short knife at the belt and a rough wooden cudgel.
